About this coffee

Colombia Wuchii 100% Arabica Speciality Grade Coffee

Provenance

Altitude: 1750 MASL
Location: Antioquia
Process: Washed
Variety: Castillo, Caturra, Colombia

Tasting Notes

Brown Sugar / Chocolate Digestive / Clementine

Story

Wuchii is the name Siruma gives to its introduction to regional speciality coffees. It’s a gateway through which the company broadens its speciality offering, supporting more growers with regular workshops and farm visits to strengthen their skills and help them harvest better coffee. This lot comes from Antioquia, in the mountains of Colombia’s Western Andes. It’s one of the regions where Siruma is actively building speciality supply chains, alongside Cauca, Tolima, Caldas, Huila, Risaralda and Valle del Cauca.

The region’s high elevations and cool mountain temperatures slow cherry maturation, enhancing natural sugars and developing a bright yet balanced acidity. Fertile volcanic soils and consistent rainfall support stable, high-quality yields. Small and medium-sized family farms lead cultivation, combining knowledge passed down through generations with support from Siruma’s sustainability and agronomy team. The team advises on crop management, post-harvest processing and sustainability standards.

Through this direct engagement, Siruma builds long-term relationships based on quality, transparency and shared value. It identifies regional lots that reflect the character of Antioquia’s terroir while ensuring growers receive fair value for their coffee.

Grind Guide

Whole beans
Recommended for best freshness

Espresso Fine
Suitable for home espresso machines

Moka Pot Fine
Suitable for moka pots and stove tops

Filter Medium
Suitable for V60, aeropress, chemex, kalita & clever dripper

Cafetiere Coarse
Suitable for cafetiere, french press and electric filter brewers

If you would like you’re coffee ground for a specific brew method or setting, please fill in the addional information box during checkout

How to Store your coffee

We recommend you store your coffee in a cool, dry area away from direct sunlight. Keep them in their original bag, or transfer them to an airtight container.

For the best flavour, enjoy your coffee within three months of the roast date. Avoid storing coffee in the fridge or freezer.
